transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Start: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~50 minutes
- Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Lin (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (TerraBank Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra Lead), Sofia Rivera (Security), Noah Reed (PM)

Auto-summary (brief): Discussed Dedicated capacity needs for TerraBank's fraud and customer support models, isolation and compliance requirements, burst behavior, and pilot plan.

00:00 Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Ethan who's our solutions engineer
00:12 Maya: hi ava, hi ethan, thanks. i'm maya, we run the ml platform here at terrabank. on the call today liam and sofia and noah
00:20 Ethan: awesome. quick agenda, 1) understand workloads and SLOS, 2) security/isolation reqs, 3) throughput and burst expectations, 4) next steps for a pilot
00:30 Liam: just to add, we care a lot about predictable throughput during peak windows, and we need guaranteed data isolation for some PII flows
00:40 Sofia: yes and on the security side we need k m s integration, audit logs, and sso with saml, plus SOC2 evidence
00:52 Ava: great, that's helpful context. maya can you kick off with what models you're running and the traffic profile?
01:05 Maya: sure, so we have two main real-time models: a fraud-scoring transformer, about 2b parameters quantized for inference, and a customer-chat assistant ~7b. the fraud model is the critical one for us, 95th pctl latency target is 150ms at p50 token generation, and we run about 6k qps at peak for simple scoring calls - actually.. hmm sorry 6k calls per minute, which is about 100 rps, average sequence length short ~30 tokens
01:36 Ethan: ok so 100 rps, short sequences - that fits continuous-attention workloads, good to know. what are your throughput and concurrency expectations per GPU?
01:45 Maya: we haven't fully benchmarked but looking for guidance. we prefer reserved GPUs to avoid noisy neighbors and unpredictable throttling
01:52 Ava: that's exactly where Dedicated comes in. Reserved GPU pools give you isolation and predictable throughput. we also offer 'burst capacity' for traffic spikes tied to a burst pool with documented fallback policies
02:08 Liam: how does burst work? do you spill to hosted? or to other pools? we don't want any data leaving our isolated environment
02:18 Ethan: good question. by default, dedicated burst stays within your dedicated cluster if you pre-configure burst nodes. if you opt into cross-region fallback or hosted fallback that's a policy toggle, but for customers needing full isolation we keep everything inside the private/dedicated footprint. there are options: 1) pre-warm a small burst pool, 2) autoscale with reserved+ephemeral within your dedicated tenant, 3) policy-based throttling instead of fallback
02:46 Sofia: can you confirm that if we choose dedicated and insist on no-hosted-fallback, there is no data egress to Redwood-hosted multi-tenant infra?
02:55 Ethan: yes, if you choose that strict policy, requests and KV cache remain within your dedicated capacity. we log requests to your audit logs but nothing leaves the tenant; we can show an architecture diagram in the security pack
03:05 Maya: what's the typical cold-start for autoscaling new GPUs? we see spikes at midnight batch windows and at card-not-present fraud surges
03:13 Ethan: autoscale times depend on instance type and warm pools, generally adding a cold GPU is ~90-180s, but we recommend a small pre-warmed burst pool for sub-30s latency SLOs. we also recommend prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts which cuts token work dramatically
03:34 Liam: that prefix caching — is it customer controlled? where does the KV cache live?
03:40 Ethan: KV cache is local to the serving nodes in your dedicated cluster. you control caching policies. for strict data residency, cache still resides in your tenant and can be encrypted at rest with your KMS keys
03:55 Sofia: talking of KMS, do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) / HSM? we need that for certain EU PII flows
04:02 Ava: yes, we support KMS integrations; for private deployments we support your HSM/KMS. we'll attach the security docs but in short: encryption at rest and in transit, CMKs are supported, and we have audit logs per request
04:16 Noah: curious on cost — if we reserve GPUs but also keep a warm burst pool, what's the pricing model? is burst usage billed differently?
04:25 Ava: burst nodes if reserved are billed like reserved, ephemeral burst (on-demand) has a slightly higher per-hour rate. we can send a SKU sheet with examples. there's also a unit token cost difference between hosted and dedicated due to operational overheads
04:40 Maya: can you do deterministic tail latency? we need a 99th percentile guardrail during peak promos
04:46 Ethan: we provide SLO tooling and can surface per-route 99p latencies. For strict requirements, you can pin model variants to lower-memory quantized instances to reduce variability. also automatic fallback to smaller model for best-effort---though that is a policy you opt into
05:05 Liam: how many GPUs would you recommend for 100 rps for the 2b quantized model?
05:12 Ethan: rough back-of-envelope: with quantized 2b at 30-token average and continuous batching you'll get ~150-250 requests per second per A100-class GPU depending on batch config. i recommend starting with 2-3 reserved GPUs and a 1-GPU warm burst pool for pilots, then scale after bench results. we'll provide concrete throughput numbers in the benchmark template
05:38 Maya: ok that sounds reasonable. the other big question is deployment mode: we are evaluating three options internally — Redwood Hosted, Dedicated (tenant), and Private (VPC/on-prem). for compliance we lean Dedicated or Private
05:52 Ava: understood. key differences: Hosted is fastest to get started; Dedicated gives tenant isolation plus predictable throughput; Private gives customer-managed network and full control (on-prem or VPC) and is the recommended for regulated PII workloads. we'll map features / tradeoffs in the follow-up doc
06:10 Sofia: for Private, do you offer the same autoscaling and console features? we can't lose the rollout/observability tools
06:18 Ethan: yes, Private includes the same Console features; in VPC mode the control plane remains customer-managed but observability pipeline outputs to your endpoints. there are some ops differences but feature parity is high
06:30 Maya: what about model versions and rollouts? we need canary and A/B and automatic fallback if a new model regresses fraud detection metrics
06:39 Ava: we support rollouts per model route, canary percentages, and automated fallback to previous versions if error rates or quality regress below thresholds. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and batching settings during your pilot to hit cost/latency targets
06:54 Noah: speaking of quality, do you do evals as part of the pilot? we need to ensure fraud detection AUC doesn't drop with quantized variants
07:02 Ethan: yep, we can run evals against your test sets and track regressions. our QA hooks integrate with rollouts so you can gate production with eval thresholds
07:15 Maya: timeline wise, if we sign up for a pilot, how fast to provision dedicated capacity?
07:22 Ava: provisioning reserved capacity typically takes 3-7 business days depending on region and quota. for pilots we often do a small dedicated pool and start benchmarks within 48-72 hours if quotas are available
07:34 Liam: any compliance artifacts we should expect? pen test, SOC2, ISO certs?
07:40 Ava: we'll share SOC2 attestation, pen test summary, and our security whitepaper. For Private deployments we can share more detailed architecture diagrams and assist with contract-level controls
07:50 Sofia: we'll need SAML metadata and KMS integration steps to validate with our security team
07:55 Ava: noted, i'll include SAML / KMS docs in the follow-up pack
08:01 Ethan: i'll send the benchmark template and sample workload config. if you can provide token distribution and 95/99p latency targets that'll help us size properly
08:12 Maya: we can provide sample logs and qps histograms; i'll follow up in the next couple days
08:18 Noah: ok so recap: Ava sends pricing + security docs, Ethan shares benchmark template, terrabank provides sample traffic and SLOs, then we schedule a benchmark kickoff
08:28 Ava: yep exactly. anything else before we close?
08:33 Liam: just one last question — how do you handle data retention for request logs? we have to purge after 30 days for certain flows
08:40 Ethan: retention is configurable per-route; you can set TTLs and we can also support automatic purge hooks and ensure archived logs are encrypted with your keys
08:52 Maya: great, thanks everyone, this was useful
08:55 Ava: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc pack and action items
09:00 End of recording

Notes on transcription quality: some proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., model sizes or internal feature names) — please refer to attached docs for canonical names.
file_notes: References to follow-up artifacts: (1) Dedicated SKU/pricing sheet (link to be provided), (2) Benchmark spreadsheet (Ethan), (3) Security pack (SOC2, KMS integration, SAML guide). Mentioned privacy constraints: no-hosted-fallback option to ensure tenant isolation.
